transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’ve just been feeling… restless, maybe more than I’d like to admit. It’s not like I’m falling apart or anything, but I feel wound too tight a lot of the time, like I can’t fully settle.

Even in situations where I should be calm—like sitting through a planning meeting, or when I’m painting, or even doing yoga—I still feel like there’s this motor running inside me. I don’t know if that makes sense, but that’s basically what brought me in.
How long have you been feeling this restless, 'wound up' way—days, weeks, or longer?

Longer, definitely longer. I mean, I’ve probably always had a bit of a hard time fully settling, but it’s been noticeably harder to manage for… about two years? Maybe two years and a couple months.

It seemed to get worse once the conflicts with my in-laws started taking over more of our evenings. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because we’re managing, but that’s when I really started noticing I couldn’t calm down as easily.
Have you noticed any physical changes over these two years, like unexplained weight loss, feeling unusually hot or sweaty, a racing heart, or hand tremors?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven’t noticed anything like that in a clear way. My weight’s been pretty stable, as far as I can tell, and I wouldn’t say I’m unusually sweaty or shaky or anything.

I do get keyed up, but it feels more like… internal restlessness than a physical illness thing, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?

Would you say your worry and restlessness are mainly tied to the situation with your in-laws, or do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things in your life—like health, work, or finances—even when things are going okay?

I’m not totally sure how to separate those, honestly. I mean, the in-law situation is definitely the easiest one to point to, and I don’t want to overstate it like I’m worrying about everything all the time.

I guess I do get worked up about normal life things too, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worried about health or finances when everything’s fine. It feels more like once something is on my mind, I have trouble letting my body settle down, if that makes sense. Is that answering what you’re asking?
Even on days when you're not thinking about the situation with your in-laws, do you still notice that same restless, wound-up feeling showing up in other parts of your life?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it’s not extreme, and I can usually keep it together, but that wound-up feeling does show up even when I’m not actively thinking about them.

Like I’ll be sitting in a planning meeting at work, or even doing something that’s supposed to be calming—painting, or yoga—and I still feel like I can’t quite settle. It’s like my body is a little too tightly wound, if that makes sense. I don’t know if that’s the kind of restlessness you mean.
Over these past two years, have you also noticed trouble falling or staying asleep, feeling unusually tired, or difficulty concentrating because your mind feels too keyed up?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I have normal nights where I don’t sleep perfectly, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern of not being able to fall asleep or waking up a lot because my mind is keyed up.

And I wouldn’t say I’m unusually tired either. Concentration… maybe here and there, but not in a way where I’ve thought, “Oh, this is because I’m too worried or wound up.” I can usually get through what I need to. Does that make sense?
When you notice yourself getting worried or wound up, do you find it hard to stop or control that worry once it starts?

I don’t know that I’d call it uncontrollable, exactly. I mean, I can usually redirect myself if I need to, especially if I’m at work or around other people.

Sometimes it takes me a little while to come down from it, but I wouldn’t say I’m just spiraling and can’t stop. It’s more like… I notice it, I try to move on, and eventually it passes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed increased muscle tension—like tightness in your neck, shoulders, or jaw—or found yourself becoming more irritable than usual over these past two years?

I don’t think so, not in any clear way. I mean, my shoulders can get tight sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it increasing over the last couple of years or that it’s a big pattern.

And irritability… I hope not. I’m sure I have moments where I’m a little short, like anyone, but I don’t think I’ve been more irritable than usual. At least not that I’ve noticed. Does that answer it okay?

Would you say this restless, wound-up feeling has actually interfered with your daily life—like your work, relationships, or things you enjoy—or is it more something you notice but manage to push through?

I guess… mostly I push through it, but it probably has interfered a little more than I like to admit.

At work, there have been a few purchase orders I had to correct, and my planning coordinator has started doing a bit of extra review on things, which is embarrassing. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but it has created some extra cleanup.

And at home… family dinners can get tense sometimes because I guess I talk over people without meaning to. They’ve said they feel interrupted or not really heard. I don’t mean it that way, but I can see how it comes across. Does that sound like the kind of interference you’re asking about?
